rules.title: Burst pipe or water near electrics
steps: Move everyone away from the water.
Switch off the flat's main breaker — only if you can reach it without standing in water.
Close the main inlet valve. If it is a common line, ask security to close the building valve.
Call the society admin. Call 112 for any electrical hazard or injury.
If the burst is on the road main, report it to the municipal water department.
File a complaint so the repair is tracked.

rules.title: Pipe-joint leak or wall seepage
steps: Close your flat's main inlet valve.
Unplug appliances and keep sockets near the wet wall switched off.
Photograph the spot and mark it.
File a complaint under 'leakage'.
Reopen the valve only for short periods until it is repaired.

rules.title: Dripping tap or running flush
steps: Put a container under the drip so the water is at least used.
Close the small valve under that tap or cistern, if there is one.
Replace the washer, cartridge or flush flapper, or book a plumber.
Enter it as a dripping tap in the calculator — each one wastes about 31 L a day.

rules.title: Outage over 72 hours, or someone vulnerable at home
steps: Ask the society admin to arrange a municipal or authorised tanker.
Treat tanker water before drinking it — boil for 1 minute, or use 2 drops of unscented 5–9% bleach per litre and wait 30 minutes.
Use water only for drinking and cooking until supply returns.
The society admin escalates in writing to the ward office, quoting the complaint number.
Call 112 if anyone shows signs of dehydration.

rules.title: Unannounced outage over 24 hours
steps: Ask the society admin to check tank levels and the pump.
The society admin registers a complaint with the municipal department and shares the complaint number.
Ration to at least 20 L per person per day for drinking and basic hygiene.
File an AquaWise complaint under 'no supply'.

rules.title: Short or announced outage
steps: Check the society notice board and municipal announcements for a scheduled cut.
Ask neighbours — is it only your flat, or the whole building?
If only your flat: check that your inlet valve is open.
Save stored water for drinking and cooking first — at least 7.5 L per person per day.

rules.title: Someone is ill after drinking the water
steps: See a doctor. Call 112 if symptoms are severe, or the patient is an infant or elderly.
Stop using that source entirely.
Treat all drinking water: boil at a rolling boil for 1 minute, or add 2 drops of unscented 5–9% bleach per litre and wait 30 minutes.
Tell the society admin so other residents are warned.
The society admin reports it to the municipal department.

rules.title: Water looks or smells wrong, nobody ill yet
steps: Stop drinking untreated tap water — use sealed bottled or treated water.
If it is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth, or let it settle and draw off the clear water.
Boil at a rolling boil for 1 minute, or add 2 drops of unscented 5–9% bleach per litre and wait 30 minutes. Double the bleach if it is cloudy.
Store it in clean, covered containers.
Ask the society admin to clean the tanks and test the water against BIS IS 10500.

rules.title: Whole building or area is weak
steps: Ask the society admin to check the overhead tank level and the pump.
Check the municipal supply timings for your ward.
The society admin registers a complaint with the municipal department.
Store water during supply hours.

rules.title: Whole flat is weak, neighbours are fine
steps: Check that your flat's main inlet valve is fully open.
Leak test: close every tap and watch the meter. If it still moves, follow the leakage advice.
Ask a plumber to check the inlet filter and pipes for blockage.
File a complaint under 'low pressure'.

rules.title: Only one tap or shower is weak
steps: Unscrew and clean the aerator or shower-head mesh.
Check that the valve under that fixture is fully open.
If it is still weak, book a plumber.

rules.title: Chemical, fuel or oily contamination
steps: Do not drink or cook with it — boiling will not remove chemicals.
Use sealed bottled water.
Photograph it and collect a sample in a clean bottle.
The society admin reports it to the municipal department immediately and warns residents.
If anyone is ill, call 112.

rules.title: Sewage mixing or visible matter
steps: Do not drink, cook or brush your teeth with it — use sealed bottled water.
Photograph it and collect a sample.
The society admin isolates the affected tank and reports to the municipal department immediately.
The society admin warns all residents through the dashboard.
Reuse only after tank cleaning, disinfection and a passing IS 10500 test.
If anyone is ill, follow the 'someone is ill' advice under unsafe drinking water.

rules.title: Discoloured water or sediment
steps: Do not drink it.
Run the cold tap until it clears, and collect a sample in a clean bottle.
Treat drinking water: filter if cloudy, boil for 1 minute or disinfect, then store covered.
File a complaint under 'contamination'.
The society cleans the tank and tests the water against IS 10500.
